sections.text: 200 201 Command of the Naval Forces in the Caribbean Command of the Naval Forces in the Caribbean commander, first officer, company commander, and the Personnel & Organization Advisor. After a team-building session, the new management team started fresh. The autumn was characterized by an operational deployment in response to Hurricane Matthew and judicial and integrity investigations. Aruban Militia Aruba also has the SVT. MSKSAV provided the first four months of the SVT twice. During this period, they followed a military-oriented training course at the barracks. The Aruban militia was responsible for carrying out this task. Some of the trainees completed the entire program and have already found jobs in the Aruban labor market. There are also five internship positions at MSKSAV, where they can participate for four months at the barracks and thus prepare for a role in society. Open Day Approximately 30,000 visitors enjoyed the annual open day of MSKSAV. The purpose of the open day is twofold. On one hand, it is intended to familiarize the Aruban population with the work of the Royal Netherlands Navy (including the Marine Corps), the ARUMIL, and the Caribbean Coast Guard. On the other hand, this day is meant to raise money for a good cause. The proceeds of 30,000 Aruban guilders were donated to the Fundacion Ban Uni Man Pa Cria (school breakfast) and Stichting Turtugaruba (protection of the sea turtle). 32nd Raiding Squadron (32RSQN) 32RSQN in the Caribbean (MCC) successfully fulfilled the operational annual program. This included the following exercises: An extensive MOUT training (operations in urbanized areas) lasting 14 days at Camp Lejeune in Jacksonville (North Carolina, United States), utilizing the facilities and support of the Force Recon II Marine Expeditionary Force and the US Riverine Squadron. They worked with paint ammunition and role players in various scenarios. • Reception of Force Recon, USMC for training in Aruba • HUREX (disaster exercise after hurricane) in Sint Maarten • DISTEX (general disaster exercise) in Aruba for the station ship. • Various exercises with the local security partners of the KIA (prison), KPA (Aruba Police Corps), K9 (dog teams), and the Arrest Team of the KPA. • In total, 32RSQN provided a training week in Aruba for the CIDW three times. • As a conclusion of the year, the unit conducted an exercise in Curaçao. At the end of September, Hurricane Matthew passed through the Caribbean, narrowly missing the Leeward Islands. The Aruban government requested military assistance in preparation for the possible consequences of the hurricane. The crew was ready at the barracks to provide military assistance during the passage of Hurricane Matthew. Ultimately, this proved to be only limitedly necessary. Haiti, on the other hand, was severely affected. From October 6 to 30, 32RSQN, together with the patrol ship Zr.Ms. Holland and the support ship Zr.Ms. Pelikaan, provided emergency aid to the affected island. For two weeks, the King's Company faced significant challenges during the Kings Isle exercise. In Bonaire, the men prepared by training attacks, medevacs, patrols, and 'controlling disturbances' further for their task in the West: defense of territorial integrity and maintenance of law and order.

sections.text: Command of the Naval Forces in the Caribbean Command of the Naval Forces in the Caribbean In March and October, the Training Center of the Royal Military Constabulary provided training in crowd control. Through this training, the Marine unit is prepared to assist the local police in maintaining public order as part of military assistance. The LD and the MD are thus managed under a single command to optimize operational support. The boat group Aruba made extensive use of FRISC’s. In total, there are four of the 12-meter version (Raiding Craft) and two of the 9-meter version (Support Craft Caribbean) in Aruba. The utility and necessity of the 'boat lift' have also been recognized, and an additional boat lift is expected to be realized in 2018. Infrastructure The construction of the new office building is progressing steadily. The new office building was supposed to be in use by the end of 2016, but due to gaps in planning, it has now been postponed to early 2017. Sports The Ronde van Aruba, which takes place every year in early May, has now grown into an internationally recognized running event in the Caribbean region. The 75 km race can be completed with 4- or 2-person teams or even as an individual. Every year, many military personnel and civilians from Aruba participate in the sporting event. MSKSAV is the start and finish for the event. Marine Support Point Pointe Blanche (MSTPPB) Commander: Major (majmarns) R. Witteveen In 2016, the MSTPPB further standardized the training program and worked on making operations more robust. The focus was on spreading the workload; working on robust communication; reducing single points of failure; a more flexible training program; and working with SAP. Cooperation In 2016, MSTPPB focused on strengthening partnerships. In particular, cooperation was sought with the security partners on the island. This was done, for example, by conducting observation exercises on the SSS islands. These exercises were carried out in close consultation with local security partners. The observation skills of the rotating element are one of the capabilities that the security partners do not possess but for which there is a great need. Since there is also a need for this capacity in the Windward Islands, the MSTPPB trained two individuals as Military Trackers within the permanent element at the end of 2016.

sections.text: Command of the Naval Forces in the Caribbean Command of the Naval Forces in the Caribbean Beat the Marines As a conclusion of the year and in celebration of the Corps anniversary, the sports event 'Beat the Marines' was organized for the second time in 2016. Materiel Maintenance Head: Lieutenant Commander (kltz) D. van den Bosch, MSc, MA The Materiel Maintenance (MI) department is responsible for the maintenance and management of equipment, including vehicles, vessels, shore (communication) systems, and other operational resources such as weapons and ammunition under CZMCARIB and the Director KWCARIB. sections.text: Command of the Naval Forces in the Caribbean Command of the Naval Forces in the Caribbean was supported. Personnel and Organization Advice Senior P&O advisor: Lieutenant Commander (kltz) ing. A.C.F. Melaet In the annual plan for 2016, the goal was set to take the next step towards a robust operational product. The employees of P&O Advice Caribbean shaped this, entirely in line with the objective of P&O to provide the organization with sufficient, well-motivated personnel. Timely and active personnel filling policy in good consultation with line managers and P&O CZSK, and a critical view on labor qualifications have proven essential to getting the right employee in the right place. The training backlog for SAP must not go unmentioned as a standout issue for 2016. Especially within a small organization like CZMCARIB and the great distance to the Netherlands, being trained in a timely manner before departure has repeatedly proven to be extremely important. P&O Advice Caribbean has proven to be an indispensable source of information for line managers and employees. Additionally, collaboration with HR staff of local personnel was further expanded to gain better insight into the shared issues of shortages and to provide for current and future needs to retain knowledge within the Caribbean personnel. The career counselors primarily spoke with military personnel who will regularly repatriate to the Netherlands in 2017. The discussions aimed to provide these military personnel with more clarity about their future opportunities. Unfortunately, the absence of a new service termination regulation as well as personnel shortages within the organization affected the timely provision of clarity regarding future opportunities. sections.title: Jaarboek 2016 (p.106)
sections.text: Command of the Naval Forces in the Caribbean Command of the Naval Forces in the Caribbean (CZMCARIB) was thus established, with the professionalization of the CURMIL being implemented in the formation. Protocols and procedures, particularly in HR, have largely been described, and simultaneously, the proposed organizational structure change within the HR department has been implemented. The updating of personnel files and the preparation of digital files for input were daily tasks in 2016. The year concluded with the submission of the 'Vision Note for the Future CURMIL/ARUMIL' for further decision-making, so that an action plan can be established to fix the chosen direction in the operations of CZMCARIB. The common thread for 2016 was bringing to the agenda and securing the target group of local personnel in the (existing) consultation forums. Safety and Environment In the area of Safety and Environment, the focus in 2016 was on three sub-areas. Firstly, in the context of 'safe working', efforts began to better and more structurally carry out operational and non-operational activities. In addition to the existing Risk Inventories and Evaluations, the introduction of Task Risk Analysis was new. Secondly, managing the asbestos issue within the Caribbean was central. Examples include the asbestos contamination of the obstacle course and the Operations in Urban Areas training location at MKSUF, and the removal of the asbestos-containing pipeline at MSKSAV. The inventory of hazardous substances, particularly the so-called CMR substances (carcinogenic substances), is the third sub-area that has been addressed. Based on the reported incidents, five Committees of Inquiry (CVO) have been established. Energy Saving Insight into energy consumption (water and electricity) received full attention from CZMCARIB. The costs of energy are a substantial part of the Caribbean budget. If 1% can be saved on the energy bill, it results in a saving of approximately 60,000 guilders. In the autumn of 2016, MSKSAV began a pilot project in which four air conditioning units were equipped with Plugwise Stealth Switches. The initial results indicate that the investment is recouped in two months and thereafter provides a saving of 45 guilders per month per air conditioning unit. A rollout of these Plugwise Stealth Switches across CARIB could result in significant savings. The 'Phase 3 Solar project' - the installation of 650 kW of solar panels - at MBPAR has been completed, achieving a total capacity of 1 Megawatt. MSKSAV (300 kW) and MKSUF (350 kW) also have solar panels. Through various measures, such as replacing the drinking water network, installing osmosis systems, and improving environmental awareness, the Caribbean achieved a water saving of 30% in 2016. Environment After a lengthy process, MBPAR and MKSUF received a ministerial decree from the Minister of Health, Environment, and Nature. As a result, based on the 'Curaçao 1994 Environmental Protection Act', a package of permit regulations has come into effect for both locations. Final exercise of the CURMIL at Santa Martha, Curaçao. sections.text: 210 211 Command of the Naval Forces in the Caribbean Command of the Naval Forces in the Caribbean Training In 2016, the training courses for Company Emergency Response (BHV), Defense Accident Investigation, VCA-VOL, and VMS-DEF were provided for the personnel of the CZSK, KMar, Coast Guard, and local staff. A total of approximately two hundred employees in the Caribbean participated in a training course. Services Center for Company Social Work (DC BMW) region CARIB Head: Lt. Commander (ltz1) H.J.H. Goetzee The main tasks performed by the Services Center for Company Social Work (DC BMW) in the Caribbean region include assistance, services, reporting, support after traumatic events, and crisis intervention. For the CARIB region, DC BMW, together with the Services for Spiritual Care (DGV), is responsible for notifying family announcements. DC BMW is available on a 24/7 basis for personnel and their families. On Wednesday, January 20, 2016, the Zika virus was first detected in Curaçao. Because this virus can be harmful to the unborn child, the staff of CZMCARIB immediately addressed this situation. In consultation with the Defense leadership in the Netherlands, a preliminary action plan was devised. A number of measures were established to allow women the opportunity to travel to the Netherlands. Approximately thirty pregnant women voluntarily went to the Netherlands for a certain period during their pregnancy. These were mainly partners of military personnel stationed in the West, but also some pregnant female military personnel. This situation was significant for the families, and where necessary and possible, DC BMW provided support. As long as there is no clarity, this situation will also remain relevant in 2017. DC BMW provided psychosocial assistance to employees and their families throughout the Caribbean region in 2016. Unlike the regional offices in the Netherlands, there is often a need for long-term assistance in the Caribbean region. This is partly due to the special situation of overseas postings and the inability to fall back on alternatives such as General Social Work or other forms of civil assistance. In 2016, regular work visits were made to Bonaire (KMar) and Sint Maarten to be more accessible to personnel and their families on these islands. In the context of services to commanders, information and advisory reports were prepared, and participation in the Social Medical Team of CZMCARIB and KMar took place. In October 2016, at the request of the Head of Operational Personnel Care CZSK, DC BMW organized a follow-up program in both Aruba and Curaçao for the personnel of the units involved in the emergency aid for Haiti. In 2016, there was also attention for the initiative of DC BMW to jointly address issues involving domestic violence more effectively. This year, DC BMW provided information to a number of teachers from local schools where many children of Defense employees are placed. The goal of this collaboration is to recognize signals at an earlier stage and, if necessary, to provide support. The official guidelines provided by Dutch law and the Professional Association of Social Work Professionals (BPSW) were, of course, taken into account. DC BMW is also involved in local veteran care. In the spring, a thematic meeting for veterans was organized in collaboration with the DGV at Landhuis Ascencion. In Curaçao, the 'Veterans Association Curaçao' is active; this organization represents the interests of veterans on the island. DC BMW has contact with this association to provide access to veterans residing in Curaçao from the position as a partner within the National Veterans Care System (LZV). In this context, there are also contacts with the Veterans Care Desk of the ABP in the Netherlands. Additionally, contact is maintained with caregivers from the local Mental Health Care (GGZ). Spiritual Care The Spiritual Care in the Caribbean this year consisted of Pastor J. Wójcik, Chaplain F. van Grimbergen, Humanistic Counselor Norbert de Kooter, and Chaplain P. Vlaar. The first three are based in Curaçao, while Chaplain Vlaar is stationed in Aruba. N. de Kooter replaced Humanistic Counselor R. Donker in July 2016. Donker returned to the Netherlands after four years of service in Curaçao. The spiritual caregivers go where the men and women of Defense go. And in the Caribbean, this also applies to partners, families with children, and veterans. Every first Saturday of the month, a spiritual service is held.

sections.text: Command of the Naval Forces in the Caribbean Command of the Naval Forces in the Caribbean took care, together with a number of veterans, to maintain the military cemetery on Roodeweg. On December 24, over 850 people gathered at the exercise area to celebrate this beautiful holiday together. The GV, together with the military personnel from MBPAR, contributed to a traditional and unifying celebration. Unfortunately, in 2016, a colleague from the KMar in Curaçao also passed away. The military police, with the support of the spiritual care, bid farewell to him in an impressive ceremony. GV members enjoy accompanying someone on their life journey. Literally as well, as the HuRa organized nature walks on Curaçao this year on every fourth Saturday of the month in collaboration with Grupo Biná. Additionally, the GV also participates in exercises. sections.text:
Attachments

The Assaut was held in Willemsoord and was attended by the Commander of the Navy, Lieutenant General (ltgen) R. Verkerk. It is well known that the Royal Netherlands Navy and the Royal Institute for the Navy are filled with traditions. Therefore, it must be pleasing for many naval officers to see the Assaut return this year in winter. After eleven years of the Assaut being held in spring, it was decided in 2016 to bring this annual event back to its original time in December. This year's theme was Marco Polo and the Wonders of the Orient. In just under two weeks, 't Zaaltje and the surrounding areas were transformed into an Eastern world full of wonders. From December 15 to 17, 2016, the cadets were able to showcase what they had built, learned, and developed at the KIM. Hospitality is an important part of this, and during the Assaut, the cadets successfully put this into practice. Under the leadership of Captain (ktz) P.P. van den Berg, the KIM has further professionalized its education. The formation of files and guidance of the cadets has been a focal point and continues to develop every day. As more cadets with a higher professional education/university background join, the operations have been further adjusted to provide optimal guidance in the future. This guidance must result in the delivery of officers who are immediately deployable at the Royal Netherlands Navy upon completing their training. This was again achieved in 2016.

Coast Guard Netherlands
Director: Captain (ktz) R.J. Blok MSc

The Coast Guard protects and promotes the responsible use of the North Sea and monitors the Dutch borders, but it does not do this alone. The Coast Guard operates on behalf of five ministries: Infrastructure and Water Management, Defence, Security and Justice, Finance, and Economic Affairs. In 2016, Coast Guard personnel, together with staff from the participating services – Rijkswaterstaat, Royal Netherlands Navy, Police, Customs, Royal Marechaussee, Netherlands Food and Consumer Product Safety Authority, Royal Air Force, Inspectorate for the Environment and Transport, and the State Supervision of Mines – worked for the safety (safety & security) and economic interests of our country.

Steps towards modernization
For the Coast Guard, 2016 was a busy and challenging year. A year in which important decisions were made regarding the modernization of the Coast Guard, the reorganization came into effect, and the regular Coast Guard tasks in the areas of service provision and enforcement were carried out. The decision-making for the development and acquisition of the Maritime Operations Center Coast Guard, to replace the existing Coast Guard center, was an important step towards a modern and future-oriented Coast Guard that can operate information-driven and is equipped for its tasks.

Contribution to European operation 'Triton'
FRONTEX, the European agency for the management and coordination of external borders, requested the Netherlands to deploy the Coast Guard aircraft for the European operation Triton. Therefore, in April, the Coast Guard aircraft was stationed on the Italian island of Lampedusa to conduct surveillance over the Mediterranean Sea. The task of the aircraft and its crew was to detect and map illegal migration flows from North Africa to Europe during patrol flights, so that the responsible authorities could anticipate the situation. In case of emergencies, the aircraft could be requested to contribute to search and rescue activities, in accordance with international obligations.

Search and Rescue
Drowning victims, shipwrecked individuals, or others in distress or danger are located and rescued by the Coast Guard. Coast Guard ships, helicopters, and aircraft are ready for this Search and Rescue (SAR) task 24 hours a day. The Coast Guard carries out its SAR tasks in the North Sea (in the territorial sea and within the Dutch Exclusive Economic Zone), the Wadden Sea, the IJsselmeer, the Randmeren, and the South Holland and Zeeland rivers. In 2016, 1,565 assistance and rescue operations were carried out.

Missing kitesurfer
On October 5, 2016, the Coast Guard center in Den Helder coordinated a large-scale search operation for a missing kitesurfer. Based on various data, such as current and wind, the operators determined the search plan for the rescue units. Searching continued late into the night in the hope of finding the man alive. Unfortunately, the units found the lifeless body of the kitesurfer in Krabbendijke (Zeeland).

Emergency Situations

In emergency situations on ships, the Coast Guard is called for assistance. Examples of these situations include when a ship has run aground, has had a collision, or has become unmanageable. The Coast Guard is reachable 24 hours a day via various communication lines. In 2016, 2,340 emergency and urgent reports were received, of which 538 were unintentional.

Inland Vessel Sunk

The Coast Guard Center (KWC) received a report on July 5, 2016, of a sinking inland vessel on the IJsselmeer. The KWC summoned the Coast Guard aircraft, a rescue helicopter, and six rescue boats to provide assistance. There were three people on board, who were in the wheelhouse. This had filled with water, causing one crew member to become hypothermic. The crew members were brought ashore at Stavoren and treated by ambulance personnel once there.

Coast Guard Enforcement

To ensure safe and smooth processing of maritime traffic in the North Sea, the Coast Guard supervises compliance with applicable traffic and behavioral regulations. Enforcement officers at the Coast Guard Coordination and Communication Center carry out this task. They take action based on information from computer systems or direct Coast Guard units to conduct inspections or controls and take enforcement action. Although much information is available through various automated systems, surveillance using ships, aircraft, and helicopters provides important additional (detailed) information about, for example, potentially criminal discharges of polluted wastewater or oil. In 2016, a total of 34 criminal discharges were observed according to the criteria of the Bonn Agreement Report. Customs officers and members of the Royal Marechaussee work together on board the Coast Guard patrol vessels to inspect ships in the North Sea. Together with the Netherlands Food and Consumer Product Safety Authority (NVWA), the Coast Guard checks fishing logs, catch composition, storage space, and prohibited net equipment. In 2016, 1,218 inspections were carried out, resulting in 254 criminal offenses being detected and 172 reports being drawn up. There were 36 warnings issued and 16 administrative measures taken.

SAR Operation Becomes Drug Case

A fishing boat encountered problems on the evening of January 14, 2016, during a severe storm and sent out a distress signal. Various units were immediately alerted. It was not until the course of the night that the crew could be rescued at the mouth of the Westerschelde after a joint effort by the Coast Guard, the Belgian Air Force, and the Royal Netherlands Rescue Society (KNRM). Due to the bad weather, the boat could not be towed, and the wreck washed ashore at Cadzand during the night. When Customs officers, together with the police, boarded the wreck, they made a remarkable discovery: one thousand kilograms of cocaine.

National Safety Day

Almere with the presence of emergency services from the police, fire department, Defense, GGD, KNRM, Coast Guard, and the lifeguard service. Here, the Coast Guard is in action for a rescue demonstration.

Reorganization of the Technical Domain RN (HTD)  
Project Leader: Captain (ktz) ir. J.W. Hartman  

The Royal Netherlands Navy has the ambition to remain an innovative navy in the future, even with scarce technical personnel, increasing technical complexity, and limited financial resources, while ensuring its material readiness effectively. To achieve this goal, the program for the Reorganization of the Technical Domain RN (HTD) was initiated in 2013 after thorough research. An important first step in the HTD program was the merger of the Technical Service (TD) and the Armament Technical Service (WD). This step took place on May 7, 2014. With the merger, the existing personnel was consolidated into one service, the Technical Service (TD). In 2016, various projects and trials aimed at changing the technical operations on board the operational units and streamlining training were completed, and the results were subsequently integrated into the line organization. Furthermore, the reorganization plan was established to optimally align the job profile for TD personnel with the changes brought about by the HTD program. This was done after extensive consultation with employee representation and trade unions. The implementation of the reorganization will start in 2017. With the integration of the results into the line organization and the upcoming implementation of the reorganization in 2017, the HTD program in its current form has been terminated, and the further development of the TD will be shaped within the TD committee, the advisory body of the Flag Officer Technical Service.

sections.title: Jaarboek 2016 (p.133)
sections.text: In 2016, the navy was deployed in major international operations and exercises. Prominent this year was the provision of emergency aid. After the devastating force of Hurricane Matthew, Haiti was particularly in ruins, leading to significant shortages of basic necessities. Various ships set course for the affected country to provide assistance and deliver supplies. Marines also took action to ensure that the aid could be distributed safely among the population. Additionally, the navy showcased its capabilities in the Mediterranean by rescuing migrants in perilous situations at sea. As part of drug enforcement, several ships participated in the Counterdrug Operation Carib Venture. Furthermore, participation occurred in large international exercises such as Black Alligator and Emerald Move. The maintenance program for the Walrus-class submarines continued, and the maintenance of Zr.Ms. Van Speijk was successfully completed. Personnel underwent many new training courses and participated in (international) exercises. During the World Port Days in Rotterdam, the navy was present with marines and several ships to introduce visitors to the armed forces. Cover photo: Haiti, Les Cayes, October 11, 2016. The Dutch armed forces provide emergency aid to Haiti after Hurricane Matthew has ravaged the island. Participating ships of the Royal Netherlands Navy are Zr.Ms. Holland and Zr.Ms. Pelikaan. Photo: Wherever Zr.Ms. Holland anchors, the local population gathers. YEARBOOK OF THE ROYAL NETHERLANDS NAVY
